messages.content: The forum agenda finally posted. The certification workshop is Tuesday at 1, with check-in at the convention center before that. The Tuesday DEN-MSY nonstop is about $180 less, but it lands late morning. Monday has a late-afternoon nonstop and would mean another hotel night. Mark thinks he can come Friday evening if I stay until Sunday. Can we turn this into an actual booking plan?

Yes. I’d separate it into three linked decisions: arrive Monday if protecting the certification credit matters more than the extra night; use Tuesday morning only if you’re comfortable going straight from MSY to the convention center; and pick the hotel based on whether Mark joins. If he is likely, the Warehouse District option gets stronger for the weekend. Do you have the exact Tuesday landing time and check-in window?

Tuesday flight leaves Denver at 7:15 and lands 10:55. Check-in says 11:30 to 12:30. The Monday flight I’d actually take leaves around 4:40 and lands a little after 8. So Monday is cleaner, but it’s the fare difference plus one more night.

On Tuesday, even an on-time arrival is tight: deplane, get to rideshare pickup, drive 25 to 35 minutes into town, and find convention check-in. That can work with a carry-on and a calm day, but a 45-minute delay turns it into a sprint. Monday arriving after 8 p.m. is less convenient, but it makes Tuesday controlled.
The certification credit is confirmed. I don’t want to blow that, but I also don’t want to make this more expensive than it needs to be.

If the credit is important, Monday is the safer recommendation. If you decide the Tuesday savings are worth it, I’d only do it with two guardrails: no checked bag, and go directly to the convention center rather than trying to stop at the hotel. I would not add a connection just to reduce the fare.

Hotel details: official block is $239 and convenient but sounds busy; CBD is $215, 4.6 rating, quieter, gym only; Warehouse District is $229, 4.4 rating, pool, hot tub, and a real fitness center, but no useful shuttle.

Given Mark is likely for Friday night, I’d rank them: 1) Warehouse District, because it still rates well and is better for the weekend and downtime; 2) CBD, if sleep is the only priority and you’re comfortable giving up the pool and hot tub; 3) official block, only if the conference shuttle or block convenience is worth the busier setting.
I’m leaning Warehouse District then. Keep it cancellable Tuesday through Sunday, and if Mark’s plans fall apart I can still decide whether to shorten?

Yes. Book a cancellable Tuesday-through-Sunday reservation, ideally one room for the whole stay so you do not have to change rooms before the weekend. Add Mark as an additional guest once he’s definite, and request a quieter room away from elevators and street noise.
Would you still tell me to arrive Monday, or is Tuesday acceptable enough to book now?

My recommendation is Monday if you want the certification day protected. But Tuesday is acceptable if you’re consciously accepting the timing risk for the savings and keeping the logistics lean. Since check-in currently runs until 12:30 and the workshop starts at 1:00, the Tuesday nonstop is not reckless; it just has little slack.
Okay. Book Tuesday morning outbound, Sunday return, Warehouse District Tuesday through Sunday. Mark can book Friday once he has final approval. What order should I do everything in?

Do it in this order: first book the Tuesday DEN-MSY nonstop and Sunday return before the fare moves; second book the cancellable Warehouse District room for Tuesday through Sunday; third register for the certification workshop and save the check-in instructions; fourth have Mark book his Friday evening flight after his approval is firm; fifth add him to the room and note his late arrival. Put a reminder on the itinerary that Tuesday requires carry-on only and a direct rideshare from MSY to the convention center.

messages.content: We have a problem. I booked the Tuesday morning nonstop and the Warehouse District hotel like we discussed. The organizer just moved certification check-in earlier to 10:45 and said late arrivals might not be seated until a break. My flight still lands at 10:55. Do I need to change to Monday?

With that new check-in time, yes, I’d move to Monday if the cost is tolerable. Keeping Tuesday means you are late even before deplaning, airport pickup, traffic, and convention-center check-in. The only way to keep it is to go straight there with luggage and accept that you could miss the opening portion.
The Monday late-afternoon nonstop is available. Fare difference is $140. Hotel can add Monday night at the same $229 before tax. So maybe $400 all in.

For a certification workshop where the organizer specifically warned about seating, that is a defensible change. It buys you a normal Tuesday morning, no luggage issue, and no dependence on a perfect flight. I’d document that the event check-in moved earlier in case your manager asks about the added night.
What order should I change things? I don’t want to break the hotel reservation, and Mark still arrives Friday evening.

Start with the hotel: add Monday night to the existing reservation and confirm it remains one continuous stay in the same room. Then change the outbound flight to Monday late afternoon. After that, send the hotel a late-arrival note for Monday and leave Mark attached to the Friday/Sunday part of the stay.
Should I notify the conference, or just show up Tuesday morning?

Notify them briefly: 'I changed travel because of the updated check-in time and plan to check in Tuesday morning.' Ask whether materials are picked up at certification check-in or general registration. Also recheck the seat assignment after the flight change, update the rideshare plan to the hotel Monday night, and keep the Sunday return unchanged unless Mark’s approval falls through.

messages.content: Five days out from New Orleans. I changed to the Monday late-afternoon arrival, Sunday return, and the Warehouse District hotel is confirmed for the full stay. Can you sanity check the last pieces? Forecast now says heavy rain during the forum.

Trip still works better with Monday arrival. Last pieces to confirm: hotel room held for your late arrival Monday, front desk or bell desk options if anything goes sideways, Tuesday shuttle times to the convention center, and whether rideshare is smarter in rain. Also verify conference QR or ID, certification materials, and Mark’s Friday arrival details.
Hotel has my late arrival noted. I haven’t asked about luggage storage. Since I’m arriving Monday, is that still a thing?

Less critical now, but ask anyway. You may need storage Sunday after checkout if your return is later, or as a backup if the room has an issue Monday night. Also ask whether they hold bags for Mark if he gets in before you’re back from a Friday event.
The hotel advertises a convention shuttle, but it’s not super clear. Should I rely on that Tuesday morning?

Only if they can give you a specific departure that reaches the convention center at least 30 minutes before certification check-in. In heavy rain, a vague loop shuttle is risky. If the schedule is not firm, use rideshare Tuesday morning and save the shuttle for lower-stakes trips back.
Mark lands Friday around 7:20 p.m. He still needs a seat, and I should check mine after the flight change. Window if possible for both of us.

Check both today. For you, make sure the Monday outbound change did not drop your seat and select a window if one is open. For Mark, pick a window now rather than waiting for check-in; if only paid windows are left, compare the fee against how long the flight is before buying.
Help me keep this carry-on only. Conference clothes plus weekend walking plus rain is getting annoying.

Pack one carry-on plus a slim tote: two bottoms, three tops, blazer or cardigan, one dinner/weekend top, dark walking shoes, compact rain shell or umbrella, and a chargers pouch. Wear the bulkier shoes and jacket. Keep agenda, ID, badge QR, meds, laptop, certification papers, and any training items in the tote. Before leaving: call the hotel for storage and shuttle times, screenshot the hotel address, and have Mark send his flight and seat confirmation.
